result.title: What a Calibrated Probability Hides: Belief-Level Post-Training for Decision Models
result.summary: A calibrated decision model can predict how often each answer is chosen. The same prediction can reflect disagreement among people who are confident in their choices or uncertainty among people who share a belief. Disagreement calls for identifying whose perspective applies, while uncertainty calls for gathering more evidence. Standard post-training scores a single prediction against one observed choice at a time, learning the pooled distribution without distinguishing these two sources of uncertainty. We introduce Belief-Grouped Policy Optimization (BGPO). The policy proposes a list of beliefs, estimates their prevalence, and predicts a choice distribution for each. During training, BGPO uses Bayes' rule to estimate how likely each belief was to generate an observed choice. These estimates weight the choice's contribution to each belief's log-score reward. To discover rare beliefs, the policy also proposes lists after seeing a few observed choices and retains them only if they predict held-out choices well. At inference, the policy uses only the question and combines the belief-specific distributions by prevalence to produce a calibrated aggregate prediction. On benchmarks covering opinions, conversation safety, emotions elicited by artwork, and photo aesthetics, BGPO achieves the lowest conditional, worst-group, and overall Jensen-Shannon divergence across model initializations. It improves conditional divergence on both text and image tasks. On a synthetic image task with known beliefs, BGPO recovers the underlying groups more accurately than baselines trained with belief labels.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Belief-Grouped Policy Optimization（BGPO）：策略先生成一组潜在信念及其占比，并为每个信念预测选择分布；训练时用贝叶斯规则估计观测选择由各信念生成的可能性来加权奖励，并以留出选择筛选稀有信念，从而区分人群分歧与个体不确定性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“多潜在信念假设＋证据加权贡献＋留出验证筛选”的机制，可能为 LVR 的多 latent 假设训练、贡献分配及证据获取与停止决策提供可核查线索，但论文未直接研究视觉推理。
